pairs.subject: concurrency-guards
pairs.evidence: crates/api/src/state.rs:193 A policy read started before an update can finish after cache invalidation and republish the old policy without checking a generation.

techniques.evidence: crates/api/src/state.rs:193 The awaited store read publishes unconditionally; invalidation neither advances a generation nor prevents an older read from restoring stale policy.

crates/api/src/projects.rs:184 Project updates read the row, modify a local copy, and replace mutable fields without a transaction or version predicate covering the read; overlapping partial updates can erase each other's changes.
crates/api/src/billing.rs:89 Webhook deduplication uses the provider and stable delivery identity rather than a per-attempt nonce.
crates/api/src/idempotency.rs:7 Billing records receive deterministic provider-derived IDs and use an upsert backstop, so cache eviction or restart does not multiply revenue rows.
crates/api/src/billing.rs:115 Failed-delivery cleanup runs only after the awaited insert returns; cancellation before that cleanup can leave an unsuccessful delivery marked seen until FIFO eviction.
crates/api/src/billing.rs:93 The seen-set conflates in-flight and completed deliveries: a second delivery receives success before the first insert commits, even if that insert subsequently fails.

pairs.subject: concurrency-guards
pairs.evidence: crates/store-pg/src/jobs.rs:125 Job progress updates check neither the lease identity nor lifecycle status, allowing an old worker to overwrite progress after reclamation or completion.

techniques.evidence: crates/store-pg/src/jobs.rs:125 Unlike finish and renewal, worker progress carries no fence and does not reject stale attempts.
crates/store-pg/src/alerts.rs:95 Delivery appends retain the row lock across the awaited read and update until transaction commit, preventing concurrent channels from losing each other's outcomes.
crates/store-pg/src/jobs.rs:69 Job acquisition uses an atomic database statement with row locking and stale-running-row reclamation, rather than process-local exclusion.
crates/store-pg/src/alerts.rs:38 Alert admission uses the same stable dedup key for its transaction-scoped advisory lock and existing-alert lookup.
crates/store-pg/src/revenue.rs:29 Revenue replay converges on the existing deterministic ID through absolute field assignments instead of additive revenue writes.
crates/store-pg/src/price_fill.rs:105 Price filling repeats its eligibility predicate in the mutation, so preparation cannot overwrite a cost established concurrently.
crates/store-pg/src/relay_lease.rs:130 Relay settlement holds a scoped SQL transaction whose drop rolls back early exits and releases its row lock; successful settlement commits explicitly.

pairs.subject: concurrency-guards
pairs.evidence: clients/typescript/src/journal.ts:191 Two recovering processes can both read an orphan journal before either deletes it and independently emit duplicate telemetry.

techniques.evidence: clients/typescript/src/admission.ts:131 Asynchronous observations overwrite each scope in arrival order without attempt attribution; an older accepted response arriving late can clear a newer refusal's retry deadline.

clients/typescript/src/instrument.ts:75 A module-global trace context is changed across an awaited callback and restored afterward without isolation, so overlapping traces can overwrite and restore each other's context.
clients/typescript/src/journal.ts:191 Orphan recovery performs stat, read, and delete without an atomic claim; concurrent processes can both collect the same records.

clients/typescript/src/index.ts:418 Recovered breadcrumbs are emitted without a stable event ID, so two recoveries of the same breadcrumb cannot converge at the server's event-ID deduplication boundary.

clients/typescript/src/index.ts:621 The shared refresh promise is cleared only after this unbounded request settles; request() supplies no timeout or abort signal, so a hung fetch can prevent every later refresh.
